rationale: A human-like hand touches Daniel's lips and he opens his mouth to speak. The Lord stretches out His hand and touches Jeremiah's mouth, putting His words there. The touch and restored or enabled speech are shared; the hand touching Daniel is not identified as the Lord's own hand.
source_text: Something like a human hand touched my lips. I opened my mouth, spoke, and said to the one standing opposite me, “My lord, something like a vision turned upon my side, upon me, and there was no strength in me.

target_units.text: The Lord stretched out His hand toward me and touched my mouth. The Lord said to me, Behold, I have put My words into your mouth.

relationship: related restorative touch from a visionary figure
rationale: The human-like figure again touches and strengthens Daniel. In the earlier vision the speaker touches and raises him from the ground. The connection concerns the restorative touch, without treating strengthening and raising as identical actions.
source_text: Again one with a human appearance touched me and strengthened me,

target_units.text: As he spoke with me, I fell asleep face down on the ground. He touched me and raised me on the spot,

relationship: close exhortation to courage rather than fear
rationale: Daniel receives commands not to fear and to take courage and be strong, becoming strong as he hears. Joshua receives the command to be strong and courageous rather than afraid. Joshua's commission to lead Israel is different from Daniel's reception of a vision.
source_text: and said to me, “You are a man worthy of pity. Do not fear; be well. Take courage and be strong.” As he spoke with me, I became strong and said, “Let my lord speak, for he has strengthened me.”

target_units.text: Behold, I have commanded you: be strong and courageous. Do not be fainthearted or afraid, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”

relationship: same-chapter resumption of the conflict with the Persian king's general
rationale: The speaker says he will return to contend with the general already described as resisting him for twenty-one days. The new mention of the Greek general extends the account; neither general is renamed as a particular demon or historical monarch.
source_text: He said to me, “Do you know why I came to you? Now I will return to contend with the general of the king of the Persians. I was going out, and the general of the Greeks was coming in.

target_units.text: The general of the king of the Persians stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the foremost rulers, came to help me, and I left him there with the general of the king of the Persians.”

relationship: related accounts of Michael's angelic role
rationale: Michael is called the angel who alone helps the speaker in the conflict. The later account calls Michael the great angel standing over the sons of Daniel's people. The common named angel connects the passages in their different roles, without changing either title to an unstated one.
source_text: I will indeed show you the first things in a record of truth. No one was helping with me concerning these except Michael the angel.”

target_units.text: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.

relationship: close reprise of the encouragement given to Daniel
rationale: The first-year notice says he was told to be strong and take courage. The preceding account records the corresponding words and Daniel becoming strong as they are spoken. The source's Cyrus dating is retained rather than replaced with Darius.
source_text: In the first year of King Cyrus, he told me to be strong and take courage.

target_units.text: and said to me, “You are a man worthy of pity. Do not fear; be well. Take courage and be strong.” As he spoke with me, I became strong and said, “Let my lord speak, for he has strengthened me.”

relationship: close shattering and four-wind division of dominant rule
rationale: The kingdom is shattered and divided toward heaven's four winds, not according to the former ruler's might. The goat's great horn is likewise shattered and followed by four horns toward those winds. This compares the stated structural pattern without assigning the unnamed ruler a historical identity.
source_text: When he arises, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, not according to his might or the lordship with which he ruled. His kingdom will be removed, and he will teach others these things.

target_units.text: The male goat grew exceedingly strong. When it became strong, its great horn was shattered, and four other horns rose behind it toward the four winds of heaven.

relationship: same-chapter repetition of a plant arising from a root
rationale: The source introduces a plant from his root, and the later unit introduces a royal plant from his root. The repeated succession imagery is explicit; the persons and the military or nonmilitary outcomes are not treated as identical.
source_text: A plant from his root will arise on its own, and the king of the north will come against his force with his strength, cause turmoil, and prevail.

target_units.text: From his root a royal plant will arise, a man striking a king’s glory. In the last days he will be shattered, but not in wrath or war.

relationship: related humiliation of gods and images amid conquest
rationale: The source places overthrown gods and cast images beside captives and valuables taken to Egypt. Isaiah describes Bel and Dagon's images as burdens on animals and says they themselves are led captive. The shared humiliation of images does not identify the gods or destination as the same.
source_text: He will overthrow their gods together with their cast images, and they will carry their crowds, with their precious vessels, silver, and gold, captive to Egypt. There will be a year for the king of the north.

target_units.text: Bel fell; Dagon was shattered. Their carved images became a burden for wild and domestic animals. Lift them, bound together, as a load for one who is weary
and hungry and exhausted, without strength at all; they cannot be saved from war, and they themselves were led captive.

relationship: related exaltation of heart accompanying conquest
rationale: The source joins possession of an assembled force with an exalted heart and further turmoil. Maccabees describes Alexander's conquests and spoils followed by his exaltation and lifted heart. The comparison concerns the response to power, not identification of Daniel's unnamed victor as Alexander.
source_text: He will take the assembled force, and his heart will be exalted. He will throw many into turmoil and will not be afraid.

target_units.text: He passed through to the ends of the earth and took the spoils of a multitude of nations. The earth became quiet before him; he was exalted, and his heart was lifted up.

relationship: close descriptions of unresisted power acting according to its will
rationale: The one coming against his opponent acts as he wills and faces no resistance. The ram likewise meets no animal able to stand before it and does as it wishes. The shared assertions of unopposed power do not identify the actors or rename the source's country as a particular holy land.
source_text: The one coming against him will act according to his will, and no one will resist before him. He will stand in the country, and everything will be accomplished in his hands.

target_units.text: After this I saw the ram charging eastward, northward, westward, and southward. No animals stood before it, and no one rescued from its hands. It did as it wished and was exalted.

relationship: related collapse and disappearance of an exalted power
rationale: The ruler turns to strengthen his country but stumbles, falls and is not found. The psalm describes an ungodly person raised like Lebanon's cedars, then gone so that his place cannot be found. Both contrast apparent strength with disappearance, without sharing a named individual.
source_text: He will turn his face to strengthen his country, but stumble, fall, and not be found.

target_units.text: I saw an ungodly person raised high and lifting himself like the cedars of Lebanon.
I passed by, and behold, he was gone; I sought him, but his place could not be found.

relationship: related root-and-plant imagery for an emerging leader
rationale: Daniel calls the new figure a royal plant arising from a root. Isaiah describes a shoot and blossom from Jesse's root that receives God's Spirit and judges. Jesse is named only in Isaiah; the source's shattered royal plant is not identified with that figure.
source_text: From his root a royal plant will arise, a man striking a king’s glory. In the last days he will be shattered, but not in wrath or war.

target_units.text: And a shoot will come from the root of Jesse, and a blossom will rise from the root.
And the Spirit of God will rest upon him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and godliness.
The spirit of the fear of God will fill him. He will not judge according to appearance, nor reprove according to report;
but he will judge the cause of the lowly, and reprove the lowly of the earth; and he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth, and with breath through his lips he will slay the ungodly.

relationship: related deceit in a covenant setting
rationale: Daniel describes false action in a covenant setting involving a very small and a strong nation. Gibeon's representatives act craftily with worn supplies and request a covenant. The comparison concerns treaty deception, not identical participants or a population comparison asserted by Joshua.
source_text: With the covenant and a people arrayed with him, he will act falsely and act against a strong nation with a very small nation.

target_units.text: They too acted craftily. They came, provisioned and prepared themselves, and took old sacks on their donkeys and old wineskins, torn and tied up,
with the soles of their footwear and their sandals old and patched on their feet, and worn clothing on them. Their bread for the journey was dry, mouldy, and eaten away.
They came to Joshua at Israel’s camp in Gilgal and said to Joshua and Israel, “We have come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us.”

relationship: related false speech within an outwardly sociable encounter
rationale: The two kings eat at one table while speaking falsely. Jeremiah describes peaceful speech to a neighbor while enmity remains within. Both juxtapose a sociable encounter with deceptive speech; the target does not describe the kings' meal or its appointed outcome.
source_text: Two kings alone will dine together, eat at one table, and speak falsely, but they will not prosper, for completion still awaits its appointed time.

target_units.text: Their tongue is a wounding missile; the utterances of their mouth are deceitful. One speaks peaceful things to his neighbor, and within himself he holds enmity.

relationship: related return with wealth and hostility toward Israel's holy order
rationale: Daniel's ruler returns with money and a heart against the holy covenant. Maccabees describes Antiochus returning after striking Egypt, plundering the sanctuary and going to his own land with its wealth. This is a bounded narrative comparison, not a proved identification of the unnamed ruler or an exact chronology.
source_text: He will return to his country with much money, his heart against the holy covenant. He will act and return to his country

target_units.text: After striking Egypt, Antiochus returned in the one hundred and forty-third year. He went up against Israel and came up to Jerusalem with a heavy force.
He arrogantly entered the sanctuary and took the golden altar, the lampstand for light and all its utensils,
the table of presentation, the libation vessels, the bowls, the golden censers, the curtain, the crowns, and the gold ornament on the front of the temple. He stripped everything off.
He took the silver, the gold, the precious vessels, and the hidden treasures that he found.
Having taken everything, he went away to his own land. He committed bloodshed and spoke with great arrogance.

relationship: close language of abandoning the holy covenant
rationale: Daniel says the ruler considers those who abandoned the holy covenant. Maccabees describes people adopting foreign customs, abandoning that covenant and joining the nations. The connection concerns the stated defection; it does not identify or reconstruct the source's Roman intervention.
source_text: Romans will come, drive him out, and rebuke him. He will return, become angry against the holy covenant, act, and return. He will consider them because they abandoned the holy covenant.

target_units.text: In those days lawless sons came out of Israel and persuaded many, saying, “Let us go and make a covenant with the nations around us, because since we separated ourselves from them, many evils have overtaken us.”
The proposal was good in their eyes.
Some of the people eagerly went to the king, and he gave them authority to follow the ordinances of the nations.
They built a gymnasium in Jerusalem according to the customs of the nations
and made foreskins for themselves. They abandoned the holy covenant, yoked themselves to the nations, and sold themselves to do evil.

relationship: close cluster of sacrifice suppression, sanctuary defilement and an abomination
rationale: Daniel links defiling the sanctuary, removing sacrifice and establishing an abomination of desolation. Maccabees records commands suppressing sanctuary offerings and defiling the holy place, followed by the installation of an abomination. The shared cluster is explicit without equating all numerical periods or unnamed actors.
source_text: Arms from him will arise, defile the sanctuary of fear, remove the sacrifice, and establish an abomination of desolation.

target_units.text: to prevent whole burnt offerings, sacrifice, and libation in the sanctuary, to profane sabbaths and festivals,
to defile the sanctuary and holy people,
to build pagan altars, sacred precincts, and shrines for idols, and to sacrifice pigs and unclean livestock,
to leave their sons uncircumcised, and to make themselves abominable through every uncleanness and profanation,
so that they would forget the law and change all the ordinances.
Whoever did not act according to the king’s command was to die.
In accordance with all these commands he wrote to his whole kingdom. He appointed overseers over all the people and commanded the cities of Judah to sacrifice, city by city.
Many of the people gathered to them, everyone who abandoned the law, and they did evil in the land.
They drove Israel into hiding in all their places of refuge.
On the fifteenth day of Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-fifth year, he built an abomination of desolation upon the altar. They built pagan altars in the surrounding cities of Judah.

relationship: related strength amid attacks on the covenant
rationale: Against the source's covenant-defiling setting, people who know these things become strong and act. Maccabees describes Israelites standing firm, refusing defiling food and choosing death rather than profane the holy covenant. Daniel's know-these-things wording is not changed to a conventional know-God phrase.
source_text: In sins against the covenant they will defile with a harsh people, but the people who know these things will be strong and act.

target_units.text: Many in Israel stood firm and fortified themselves against eating unclean things.
They chose to die so that they would not be defiled by foods or profane the holy covenant, and they died.

relationship: related descriptions of understanding people instructing and appearing as heavenly lights
rationale: The thoughtful of the nation give understanding to many while suffering sword, captivity and plunder. The later vision compares those who understand to heaven's lights and those who strengthen the words to the stars of heaven. This compares their intellectual and verbal role and contrasting fates without supplying individual names.
source_text: The thoughtful of the nation will give understanding to many. They will stumble by the sword and grow old in it; in captivity and plunder they will be stained for days.

target_units.text: Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.

relationship: close purification and understanding language
rationale: Some who understand consider purification, selection and cleansing toward completion. The later account says many are tested and made holy, while those understanding pay attention. The relationship preserves the distinction between their actions and what is done to them.
source_text: Some of those who understand will consider how to purify themselves, be selected, and be cleansed until the time of completion, for the time still awaits its hours.

target_units.text: many are tested and made holy, and sinners sin. None of the sinners will understand, but those who understand will pay attention.

relationship: close descriptions of exaltation above every god
rationale: Daniel's king is exalted above every god and speaks against the God of gods. The letter describes the man of lawlessness exalting himself above everything called god or worshiped. The striking shared posture does not by itself prove a common historical identity; the target additionally describes his seat in God's sanctuary.
source_text: The king will act according to his will, become enraged, and be exalted above every god. He will speak extraordinary things against the God of gods and prosper until the wrath is completed, for completion is coming upon him.

target_units.text: Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
who opposes and exalts himself above everything called god or an object of worship, so that he takes his seat in God’s sanctuary, displaying himself as being God.

relationship: related worship of gods unknown to the fathers
rationale: The source's ruler honors a god his fathers did not know with precious materials. Deuteronomy condemns sacrifice to new gods unknown to the fathers. The unfamiliar cult is the shared feature; the source does not itself call its god a demon as the target does.
source_text: He will stir in his place and honor a god whom his fathers did not know with gold, silver, and costly stone. And with the desirable things

target_units.text: They provoked Me with foreign gods; with their abominations they embittered Me.
They sacrificed unto demons, and not unto God, unto gods whom they did not know; new ones, lately come, whom their fathers did not know.

relationship: related association of Egyptian power with Ethiopia and Libya
rationale: Daniel joins control of Egypt's wealth with Libyans and Ethiopians in the ruler's multitude. Nahum names Ethiopia and Egypt as strength and Libyans as helpers for Amon. The same named regional peoples appear in different descriptions of power and defeat, not an asserted identical campaign.
source_text: He will control the place of gold, the place of silver, and all Egypt’s desirable wealth; Libyans and Ethiopians will be in his multitude.

target_units.text: Prepare a portion; tune a string; prepare a portion, Amon, who dwells among rivers, water around her, whose dominion was the sea and whose walls were water,
and Ethiopia was her strength, and Egypt, and there is no limit to the flight; Libyans became her helpers.

She too will go into deportation as a captive; they will dash her infants to the ground at the head of all her roads, cast lots for all her glorious things; and all her nobles will be bound in handcuffs.

relationship: close description of unprecedented affliction
rationale: Daniel announces an affliction unlike any since the people came into being. Jesus describes great affliction unlike any from the world's beginning. Their comparison points differ, and Daniel's concluding promise says those inscribed in the book will be exalted, not simply an imported saved wording.
source_text: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.

target_units.text: For then there will be great affliction such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, and certainly will never happen again.

relationship: related divine book distinguishing persons in judgment
rationale: Daniel connects being inscribed in the book with exaltation in the day of affliction. Moses asks to be blotted from God's book if the people's sin is not forgiven, and God speaks of blotting out sinners. The inscription-and-judgment connection does not make exaltation and erasure the same action.
source_text: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.

target_units.text: Now, if Thou wilt forgive their sin, forgive it; but if not, blot me out of Thy book which Thou hast written.”
The Lord said to Moses, “If anyone has sinned before Me, I will blot him out of My book.

relationship: related naming of Michael as a prominent angel
rationale: Daniel calls Michael the great angel standing over the people's sons; Jude names Michael the archangel. Both give the named figure an angelic role, while Jude's dispute over Moses' body differs from Daniel's day of affliction.
source_text: “At that hour Michael will pass by, the great angel who stands over the sons of your people. That will be a day of affliction such as has not occurred since they came into being until that day. On that day all the people found inscribed in the book will be exalted.

target_units.text: But Michael the archangel, when he was contending with the devil and disputing about the body of Moses, did not dare to bring a slanderous judgment against him, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you.”

relationship: close resurrection with differing outcomes
rationale: Daniel describes sleepers in the earth arising, with everlasting life, reproach, and dispersion and everlasting shame stated in three phrases. Jesus describes those in tombs coming out to resurrection of life or judgment. The shared resurrection and differing outcomes are clear without flattening Daniel's three-part wording into the target's two alternatives.
source_text: Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.

target_units.text: Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear His voice
and come out: those who did good things to a resurrection of life, but those who practiced base things to a resurrection of judgment.

relationship: close awakening of the dead from the earth
rationale: Daniel's sleepers in the earth arise; Isaiah says the dead rise, those in tombs awaken and those in the earth rejoice. Isaiah additionally contrasts the falling earth of the ungodly, while Daniel expressly describes reproach and everlasting shame.
source_text: Many of those sleeping in the breadth of the earth shall arise: some unto everlasting life, others unto reproach, and others unto dispersion and everlasting shame.

target_units.text: The dead will rise, those in the tombs will be awakened, and those in the earth will rejoice, for the dew from Thee is healing to them; but the earth of the ungodly will fall.”

relationship: close heavenly-light imagery for the honored faithful
rationale: Daniel compares those who understand to heaven's lights and those who strengthen the words to heaven's stars. Jesus says the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. The imagery of luminous honor is shared, while the source does not use the conventional turning-many-to-righteousness wording.
source_text: Those who understand will appear like heaven’s lights, and those who strengthen my words like the stars of heaven for the age of the age.

target_units.text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Let the one who has ears hear.

relationship: related sealed-book imagery restricting access to words
rationale: Daniel is told to cover the commands and seal the book until completion. Isaiah likens the sayings to a sealed book that the literate recipient cannot read, followed by an illiterate recipient. The shared closure does not replace Daniel's madness and injustice with a promise of increasing knowledge.
source_text: But you, Daniel, cover the commands and seal the book until the time of completion, until the many go mad and the earth is filled with injustice.”

target_units.text: All these sayings will be for you like the words of this sealed book. If they give it to a person who knows how to read, saying, “Read these,” he will say, “I cannot read, for it is sealed.”
This book will be given into the hands of a person who does not know how to read. Someone will say to him, “Read this,” and he will say, “I do not know how to read.”

relationship: close question about visionary completion and cleansing
rationale: Daniel asks the linen-clothed figure when the wonders will be completed and cleansed. Earlier a holy one asks how long the sanctuary's desolation remains and receives an answer ending in cleansing. The speakers and stated numerical periods are distinguished.
source_text: I said to the one clothed in fine linen above, “When, then, will the wonders you have told me reach completion, and these things be cleansed?”

target_units.text: I heard another holy one speaking, and the other said to the speaking Phelmouni, “How long will the vision stand, and the sacrifice that was removed, and the sin of desolation that was given, and the holy places be made desolate for trampling?”
He said to him, “Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days; then the sanctuary will be cleansed.”

relationship: close heavenly hand-raising and oath by everlasting life
rationale: The linen-clothed figure raises both hands to heaven and swears by the God who lives forever. In Deuteronomy God raises His hand heavenward, swears by His right hand and declares that He lives forever. The shared oath form does not identify the linen-clothed speaker as God or erase the one-hand/two-hand distinction.
source_text: I heard the one clothed in fine linen above the river’s water say, “Until the time of completion.” He raised his right hand and his left to heaven and swore by God who lives for ever that in a time, times, and half a time would be the completion of the “hands of release” of a holy people, and all these things would be completed.

target_units.text: For I will lift My hand unto heaven, and swear by My right hand, and say, I live for ever.

rationale: Daniel says he heard but did not understand the time and asks the figures' interpretation. Earlier he is undone by the vision and says no one understood. Both record limits of understanding rather than authorizing a confident solution of every time and symbol.
source_text: I heard, but did not understand the time from him. I said, “My lord, what is the interpretation of this word, and what do these figures concern?”

target_units.text: I, Daniel, was weak for many days. Then I rose and again conducted royal affairs. I was undone by the vision, and there was no one who understood.

target_units.text: and after being disciplined a little, they will receive great benefits, because God tested them and found them worthy of Himself.

relationship: close reprise of removed sacrifice and an abomination of desolation
rationale: The concluding duration begins with removal of sacrifice and preparation to set up the abomination. The earlier account joins removal of sacrifice with establishment of that abomination. The recurrence explains the stated starting conditions without converting the 1,290 days into an external calendar.
source_text: From when the sacrifice is removed for all time and preparations are made to set up the abomination of desolation: one thousand two hundred ninety days.

target_units.text: Arms from him will arise, defile the sanctuary of fear, remove the sacrifice, and establish an abomination of desolation.

relationship: close blessing upon perseverance
rationale: Daniel calls blessed the person who perseveres to the specified total of days. James calls blessed the person enduring a trial and says the approved person will receive the promised crown of life. Both connect blessing with endurance; James supplies no equivalent to the 1,335-day total.
source_text: Blessed is the one who perseveres and reaches a total of one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.

target_units.text: Blessed is the man who endures a trial, because, having been approved, he will receive the crown of life that He promised to those who love Him.

relationship: related rest followed by rising into the promised future
rationale: Daniel is told to rest and arise to his glory at the completion of days. The letter describes those who have fallen asleep and says the dead in Christ will rise at the Lord's coming. The connection concerns rest and resurrection hope without inserting the target's detailed sequence into Daniel's personal promise.

target_units.text: But we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, concerning those who are sleeping, so that you may not grieve as the rest do, who have no hope.
For if we believe that Jesus died and rose, so also God, through Jesus, will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep.
For this we say to you by a word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the Lord’s coming, will certainly not precede those who have fallen asleep.
For the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a commanding cry, with an archangel’s voice and with God’s trumpet, and the dead in Christ will rise first.
Then we who are alive, who remain, will be caught up together with them in clouds to meet the Lord in the air; and so we will always be with the Lord.
